messages.author: fecbe3dc811bed89
messages.subject: Stabilize estimation of covariance matrix?
parts:
Hi Phil,

I got a data where 1-14, 15-28, 29-42, 43-56, 57-70 items respectively measuring 5 traits. I once had estimate the covariance matrix one year ago, it looks fine at that time.
Now, I use the newer version but got different and unstable estimates. Run by

cmod <- mirt(data, cmodel, itemtype='Rasch', SE=TRUE, method = "MHRM", SE.type="", technical=list(BURNIN=1000,SEMCYCLES=200,NCYCLES=10000))

See results from "cmod" in file.

load("test")
est = coef(cmod, printSE = TRUE, as.data.frame = TRUE) # item estimates

I know it is unstable due to sparse 1 responses compared to 0 responses for second and forth traits. And, I am curious why older mirt is more stable.

Is it possible to get stable estimates (configure the MHRM setting)?  Thanks!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Stabilize estimation of covariance matrix?
parts:
This was larger due to modifying the default gain constants a while back, which also are used when computing the information matrix. To get a more accurate estimate by taking more draws just use technical = list(SEtol = .0001) to make the information matrix run longer which should help it stabilize.

Phil
